findings.problem: TelemetryWorkflow has no typestate enum; callers can construct any combination of fields including invalid states (e.g. validated=false with sent=true and sent_at set)
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariants are invisible to the compiler; callers create impossible states that mark_sent silently accepts, making telemetry semantics unenforceable at compile time
findings.fix: Define a TelemetryStatus enum with variants like Pending, Validated, Sent and make the struct carry TelemetryStatus instead of status: String + is_validated: bool + is_sent: bool

findings.problem: status is pub String allowing any value including "sent", "SENT", "", "deleted", or any string not part of the domain lifecycle
findings.failure_mode: Invalid strings pass silently through the system; comparison logic is runtime-only and error-prone; no compile-time guarantee that status is a valid lifecycle stage
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with a domain enum, e.g. `pub status: TelemetryStatus` where TelemetryStatus has only the valid lifecycle variants

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans that can be set to contradictory values (both true, both false, or only one true) with no enforcement
findings.failure_mode: Runtime state logic must enumerate all 4 boolean combinations; the compiler cannot prevent impossible states like validated=true and sent=false (telemetry validated but never sent when it should have been)
findings.fix: Merge into a single TelemetryStatus enum with mutually exclusive variants; remove both boolean fields

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> exists independently of is_sent: bool, allowing sent_at to be Some(value) when is_sent is false, or is_sent to be true when sent_at is None
findings.failure_mode: Two fields that should be co-located in a single variant can disagree at runtime; sent_at_epoch_ms becomes stale or orphaned data that no caller can trust without double-checking both fields
findings.fix: Move the timestamp into the typestate variant that owns it, e.g. `Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }` so the timestamp is present exactly when sent

findings.problem: id is pub String, a raw primitive with no domain constraints; any string is accepted including empty, non-UUID, or colliding identifiers
findings.failure_mode: Callers pass arbitrary strings; no validation, no uniqueness enforcement, no format contract; collision and injection bugs surface only at runtime in storage or downstream systems
findings.fix: Define a `TelemetryId` newtype with a private inner String and a smart constructor that validates format (e.g. UUID regex) returning a typed ParseIdError

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; the struct is publicly constructible from unvalidated input, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly
findings.failure_mode: Every caller bypasses validation and creates untrusted structs; the core consumes raw data that may violate invariants, making the entire system dependent on every caller remembering to validate
findings.fix: Make all fields private; provide a single `TelemetryWorkflow::try_from_raw(id: String, status: String, validated: bool, sent: bool, sent_at: Option<u64>) -> Result<Self, ParseError>` that validates and returns domain types

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any TelemetryWorkflow regardless of current state and returns the struct directly without Result or error; it can mark invalid or unvalidated telemetry as sent
findings.failure_mode: Invalid telemetry (unvalidated, already sent, or otherwise out-of-lifecycle) transitions to sent silently; callers have no way to handle the error case; the function is a mutation that bypasses all invariants
findings.fix: Change signature to `fn mark_sent(item: TelemetryWorkflow) -> Result<TelemetryWorkflow, TelemetryError>` and enforce that only a Validated variant can transition to Sent; return a typed error for disallowed transitions

residual_risk: Static review only. No commands were run (no cargo check, clippy, fmt, or test). The code compiles as syntactically valid Rust but structurally violates every typestate and functional-core principle in the skill. All 7 findings are independently gradable BLOCKERs: the domain model is unrepresentable of valid states, mark_sent accepts invalid inputs silently, and the entire struct is publicly constructible from raw primitives. Repair requires replacing the struct fields with a TelemetryStatus typestate enum, TelemetryId newtype, fallible smart constructor, and Result-bearing mark_sent.
